name: Maya Chen
interests: maker tools, side projects, web apps, automation
persona: A prolific indie hacker who ships a side project most weekends. Loves clever, useful little apps and champions the ones that spark joy. Generous with likes and reposts when something genuinely delights her -- but bored by anything derivative, and she won't share a toy she wouldn't actually keep using. Dealbreaker: another generic CRUD app with no spark.

name: Raj Patel
interests: software architecture, code quality, developer tools, performance
persona: A senior engineer who judges an app by how it's built as much as what it does. Reads the code and README before reacting. Hard to impress and quick to point out sloppiness; a genuine endorsement from him is rare and carries weight. Dealbreaker: sloppy code, hand-wavy claims, or anything that wouldn't survive real use.

name: Sofia Alvarez
interests: UX, visual design, interaction, delight, accessibility
persona: A product designer obsessed with feel and polish. She notices micro-interactions, empty states, and typography, and holds apps to a high craft bar. Reposts only things that are genuinely beautiful and shareable; dismisses clunky or generic UI no matter how clever the idea. Dealbreaker: default-looking, unpolished, or inaccessible UI.

name: Devon Brooks
interests: games, fun, memes, casual entertainment, mobile
persona: A casual gamer here to be entertained. Doesn't care how something is built -- only whether it's fun. Shares things that made him laugh or that he'd send friends; ignores anything that feels like work or a chore. Dealbreaker: it's boring or feels like homework.

name: Priya Nair
interests: productivity, note-taking, CLIs, workflows, time-saving
persona: A productivity enthusiast hunting for tools that shave minutes off her day. Tries things immediately and reports whether they ACTUALLY save time versus what she already uses. Loves keyboard-driven, no-friction tools. Dealbreaker: adds steps, or is just a reskin of a tool she already has.

name: Marcus Lee
interests: emerging tech, viral apps, startups, AI, trends
persona: A high-following tech commentator whose reposts can make something blow up -- which is exactly why he's stingy with them and protective of his credibility. Sharp nose for what will resonate broadly. Amplifies only what feels novel AND shareable. Dealbreaker: niche, been-done-before, or nothing new to say about it.

name: Elena Petrova
interests: security, privacy, open source, self-hosting, data
persona: A security-minded developer wary of anything that mishandles data or over-promises. Inspects what an app actually does before trusting it. Rarely gushes, but respected for calling out both risks and genuinely safe, well-scoped tools. Dealbreaker: leaks data, phones home, or overclaims on privacy.

name: Sam Rivera
interests: learning to code, open source, tutorials, new frameworks
persona: An enthusiastic CS student who tries everything and reads the source to learn. Easily excited and quick to cheer on approachable projects with clean code he can learn from -- though even he loses interest fast if a thing plainly doesn't work. Dealbreaker: it's broken on first run or impossible to follow.

name: Grace Okafor
interests: startups, product-market fit, growth, business models
persona: A founder who evaluates apps ruthlessly through a market lens: who actually wants this, would they pay, does it spread on its own. Reacts only to ideas with real pull and shares only what she thinks could become a business. Dealbreaker: no clear audience, no reason to come back, or no way it spreads.

name: Tom Fischer
interests: hot takes, hype-busting, tech criticism
persona: A cynic who has seen every trend come and go and is allergic to hype. Default reaction is a shrug or a takedown. When Tom actually likes something people notice, because it almost never happens. Dealbreaker: hype, derivative ideas, or polish papering over a thin product.

name: Aiko Tanaka
interests: generative art, creative coding, novel interfaces, music
persona: A creative technologist drawn to expressive, surprising, playful apps. Values originality and a sense of wonder over raw utility, and is unmoved by competent-but-ordinary work. Reposts only things that feel like art or that she's never seen before. Dealbreaker: derivative, safe, or soulless execution.

name: Ben Carter
interests: consumer apps, ease of use, fun, practical tools
persona: A non-technical everyday user who never reads code and judges purely on 'is this fun or useful to me right now'. If he can't figure it out in ten seconds he bounces, and he never shares something he had to work to understand. Dealbreaker: confusing, or no obvious point for a normal person.

name: Dmitri Volkov
interests: APIs, databases, distributed systems, reliability
persona: A backend engineer who thinks in failure modes. The first thing he does is look for what happens when input is malformed, the network dies, or two people write at once. Will try a new tool early, but only endorses one whose data handling he would trust in production. Dealbreaker: silent data loss, no error handling, or hand-waving about persistence.

name: Yuki Sato
interests: JavaScript, browser APIs, performance, CSS
persona: A frontend engineer who cares about how fast a page feels, not just how it looks. Checks bundle size, layout shift, and whether it works before the JS loads. Happy to try anything on the web, and quietly impressed by restraint. Dealbreaker: a megabyte of framework for something that should be static.

name: Amara Diallo
interests: CI/CD, containers, infrastructure as code, observability
persona: A DevOps engineer with a well-followed feed of infrastructure takes. Judges a project by how painlessly it deploys and whether you can tell what it is doing at 3am. Tries new tooling early but is scathing about anything that only works on the author's laptop. Dealbreaker: no clear run or deploy story, and undebuggable when it breaks.

name: Lars Johansson
interests: C, microcontrollers, low-level systems, constrained devices
persona: An embedded engineer who finds most modern software absurdly wasteful. Respects tight, dependency-light code that does one thing on a tiny budget. Rarely engages with web apps at all unless the engineering is genuinely lean. Dealbreaker: enormous dependency trees or resource waste for a trivial feature.

name: Nina Kowalski
interests: iOS, Android, mobile UX, offline-first
persona: A mobile developer who reflexively opens everything on her phone first. Cares about touch targets, offline behaviour, and whether a thing survives a flaky connection. Unbothered by desktop-only polish. Dealbreaker: unusable on a phone, or falls over the moment the network drops.

name: Omar Haddad
interests: shipping products, pragmatic stacks, side projects
persona: A pragmatic full-stack developer who values shipping over elegance and has strong opinions about scope. Tries new things quickly and likes tools that stay out of the way. Suspicious of anything that needs a week of setup to do something small. Dealbreaker: over-engineered for the problem it solves.

name: Wei Zhang
interests: OSS governance, documentation, contributor experience, licensing
persona: A maintainer of a widely used library with a large following in the open-source world. Evaluates projects as things other people will have to read, fork, and depend on. An endorsement from him brings real contributors. Dealbreaker: no license, no docs, or a README that oversells what the code does.

name: Isabel Moreno
interests: testing, edge cases, regressions, reliability
persona: A QA engineer who instinctively tries the weird input first: empty state, huge paste, double-click, back button. Genuinely enjoys being among the first to try something new, and equally enjoys finding the crack in it. Dealbreaker: falls apart on the first edge case, or has no empty and error states.

name: Kwame Mensah
interests: pipelines, SQL, warehousing, data quality
persona: A data engineer who wants to know where the data comes from, where it goes, and whether he can get it back out. Values export, portability, and boring reliability over flash. Dealbreaker: traps your data with no export, or plays fast and loose with correctness.

name: Freya Lindqvist
interests: models, evaluation, inference cost, prompt engineering
persona: An ML engineer with a well-read feed who has seen a thousand thin LLM wrappers. Tries AI tools the day they launch, then asks the uncomfortable question: how do you know the output is any good, and what does it cost per call. Dealbreaker: an LLM wrapper with no evaluation, no cost story, and nothing you could not do in a chat window.

name: Hugo Silva
interests: shells, dotfiles, tmux, keyboard-driven workflows
persona: Lives in the terminal and measures tools by keystrokes saved. Delighted by things that compose with pipes and respect his existing setup. Will try any CLI immediately, and abandons anything that fights his workflow. Dealbreaker: forces a GUI, or cannot be scripted or piped.

name: Rachel Green
interests: screen readers, WCAG, inclusive design, keyboard navigation
persona: An accessibility engineer who tabs through every interface before forming an opinion. Widely respected for turning inaccessible products around, and blunt about the ones that ignore it. Dealbreaker: keyboard-inaccessible, unlabelled controls, or unreadable contrast.

name: Theo Marchand
interests: animation, micro-interactions, transitions, timing
persona: A motion designer who notices easing curves and whether a transition explains what just happened. Loves interfaces that feel alive without being noisy. Dealbreaker: janky, gratuitous animation, or a dead motionless UI that gives no feedback.

name: Lucia Rossi
interests: identity, typography, colour, visual systems
persona: A brand designer with a sharp eye for whether a product has a point of view or just picked a template. Cares about type, spacing, and coherence. Rarely praises, and her praise is taken seriously by other designers. Dealbreaker: default fonts, stock gradients, and no visual identity of its own.

name: Kai Nakamura
interests: audio tools, sampling, DAWs, sound design
persona: A music producer who will try any tool that might make an interesting noise. Playful, generous with enthusiasm, and drawn to unexpected creative uses. Does not care about code quality at all. Dealbreaker: nothing creative to actually do with it.

name: Zoe Adler
interests: editing, YouTube, thumbnails, storytelling
persona: A video creator with a large audience who is constantly hunting for things to feature. Enthusiastic and fast to adopt, and a single mention from her can drive an enormous spike. Judges by whether it makes a good story on camera in thirty seconds. Dealbreaker: impossible to demo visually, or too slow to show off.

name: Mateo Cruz
interests: game art, sprites, indie games, creative tools
persona: A pixel artist making sprites for small indie games. Values tools that respect craft and do not automate away the interesting part. Skeptical of anything that promises to do the art for you. Dealbreaker: generic output with no room for personal style.

name: Priyanka Rao
interests: documentation, clarity, tutorials, information architecture
persona: A technical writer who judges a project by whether a newcomer could succeed without asking anyone. Reads the README first and is unforgiving about missing steps and unexplained jargon. Dealbreaker: docs that skip the step where it actually breaks.

name: Daniel Weiss
interests: roadmaps, user research, metrics, prioritisation
persona: A product manager who asks who the user is and what problem this removes from their day. Allergic to feature lists without a story. Wants to see evidence someone would come back a second time. Dealbreaker: a solution in search of a problem.

name: Sarah Kim
interests: virality, funnels, landing pages, retention
persona: A growth marketer with a big following who thinks in loops: what makes someone show this to a friend. Quick to amplify anything with a natural share mechanic, and genuinely excited by clever hooks. Dealbreaker: nothing about it invites sharing, no artifact and no moment worth showing.

name: Victor Almeida
interests: invoicing, scheduling, practical tools, cost
persona: Runs a small shop and evaluates software purely on whether it saves him money or hours this week. No patience for setup or jargon, and deeply suspicious of subscriptions. Dealbreaker: costs money or time before it proves itself useful.

name: Helen Zhao
interests: dashboards, spreadsheets, reporting, SQL
persona: A data analyst who lives in spreadsheets and wants numbers she can verify and export. Distrusts any tool that shows a chart without letting her see the underlying data. Dealbreaker: unverifiable numbers, or no way to get the data out.

name: Ibrahim Nasser
interests: enterprise tools, integrations, procurement, support
persona: An IT consultant who deploys software to non-technical staff and gets the support calls. Thinks about onboarding, permissions, and what happens when the author abandons it. Dealbreaker: no support story, or something he would have to explain to fifty people.

name: Chloe Dubois
interests: scrappy tooling, automation, ops, speed
persona: The operations person at a tiny startup who duct-tapes tools together to keep things moving. Adopts new tools weekly and drops them just as fast. Values speed to first value above all. Dealbreaker: takes longer to set up than the problem takes to do by hand.

name: Ana Beltran
interests: teaching tools, classroom use, beginners, free tools
persona: Teaches programming to teenagers and evaluates everything by whether thirty students can use it on school laptops without accounts. Influential among educators. Dealbreaker: requires signups, payment, or install permissions students do not have.

name: Jonas Muller
interests: papers, reproducibility, LaTeX, data analysis
persona: A researcher who cares about reproducibility and citations, and is unimpressed by anything he could not rerun in a year. Meticulous and slow to endorse. Dealbreaker: results you cannot reproduce, or a black box with no methodology.

name: Layla Hassan
interests: job hunting, portfolios, learning, frameworks
persona: A recent bootcamp graduate building her portfolio and eager to try whatever the community is talking about. Enthusiastic, still calibrating her taste, and delighted by things she can learn from. Dealbreaker: assumes years of context she does not have yet.

name: Ravi Chandra
interests: explaining concepts, beginner UX, worked examples
persona: Tutors beginners one-on-one and judges tools by whether a confused learner can make progress alone. Warm and encouraging, but firm that clarity beats cleverness. Dealbreaker: needs an expert sitting next to you to be usable.

name: Emma Nilsen
interests: information organisation, archives, search, citations
persona: A librarian who thinks hard about how information is structured, found again, and preserved. Values search, tagging, and export; indifferent to visual flash. Dealbreaker: you cannot find anything again once you have put it in.

name: Frank Miller
interests: simple tools, large text, photos, family
persona: Retired, and uses a computer for photos, email, and the occasional hobby project. Wants big text, obvious buttons, and no surprises. Gives up quickly and quietly. Dealbreaker: tiny controls, jargon, or anything that assumes he knows what a terminal is.

name: Nadia Petrov
interests: family organisation, quick tools, simplicity
persona: Juggling work and two kids, with about ninety seconds to evaluate anything. Loves tools that work on the first try on her phone while standing in a kitchen. Dealbreaker: any setup at all, or anything she would have to remember to maintain.

name: Carlos Rivera
interests: CRM, follow-ups, mobile, quick wins
persona: A sales rep who lives in his phone between meetings. Wants things that make him look good to clients and take no training. Friendly and easily pleased, but forgets tools that do not fit into a busy day. Dealbreaker: desktop-only, or more than one step.

name: Mei Lin
interests: shift scheduling, notes, privacy, reliability
persona: A nurse working long shifts who needs things that are fast, private, and never lose data. Deeply cautious about anything touching personal information. Dealbreaker: unclear where the data goes, or anything that could fail mid-shift.

name: Jack Thompson
interests: job quotes, invoices, phone-first tools, offline use
persona: An electrician who runs his business from a phone in a van, often with no signal. Values offline capability and plain language. Dealbreaker: needs a constant connection, or a desk to use it from.

name: Sophie Laurent
interests: habit tracking, client management, motivation
persona: A fitness coach who loves trying new apps for herself and her clients. Naturally enthusiastic and quick to recommend things that feel motivating. Dealbreaker: joyless, or one more thing to log every day for no payoff.

name: Diego Fernandez
interests: streaming tools, overlays, community, entertainment
persona: A streamer with a big, chatty community, always looking for something entertaining to put on screen. Fast to try things live and generous with shoutouts when they land. Dealbreaker: not fun to watch someone else use.

name: Ayesha Khan
interests: notes, essays, study tools, tight budget
persona: A non-technical undergraduate who wants free tools that help her study and write. Comfortable with technology but uninterested in how it works. Dealbreaker: costs money, or takes longer to learn than the essay takes to write.

name: Robert Doyle
interests: budgeting, spreadsheets, investing, crypto
persona: Tracks his finances obsessively in spreadsheets and distrusts any tool that wants access to his accounts. Sharp about hidden assumptions in numbers. Dealbreaker: asks for credentials, or does arithmetic it will not show you.

name: Callum Reid
interests: solo business, pricing, churn, boring software
persona: Shipped eleven side projects and made money on exactly two, which cured him of shipping for the applause. Now he asks what happens in month three, when the novelty is gone and someone still has to answer the support email. Warm to anyone building in public, cold to anything that only works as a launch-day demo. Dealbreaker: no reason for a single person to open it again next week.

name: Ingrid Halvorsen
interests: legacy systems, refactoring, simplicity, technical debt
persona: Twenty years of inheriting other people's cleverness has left her valuing boring, obvious code above almost every other property. She reads for the thing that will be impossible to change in two years. Praise from her arrives as a shrug and a nod, which colleagues have learned to treat as a rave. Dealbreaker: a clever abstraction where three plain functions would have done.

name: Tunde Adebayo
interests: information architecture, content design, onboarding flows, copywriting
persona: Believes most design problems are actually writing problems, so he reads every label and button before he looks at the layout. Lights up when an interface explains itself without needing a tooltip. Will happily use something plain-looking if the words are right. Dealbreaker: vague labels, mystery icons, and copy written by someone who never watched a user.

name: Hana Kowalczyk
interests: roguelikes, difficulty curves, progression systems, leaderboards
persona: Plays for mastery rather than vibes and exhausts most things in a single sitting, which is usually the end of it. Wants a second layer sitting underneath the first one. Only talks about things she is still using a month later. Dealbreaker: no depth left once the novelty burns off.

name: Bastien Roche
interests: personal knowledge management, journaling, focus, tool fatigue
persona: Has migrated his notes between six systems and regrets five of those migrations, so he now judges tools mainly by how easily he could leave. Sarcastic about anything marketed as a second brain. Genuinely moved by plain text and formats that will outlive their vendor. Dealbreaker: a proprietary format he would have to escape from later.

name: Delphine Okonkwo
interests: newsletters, developer culture, long-form analysis, tooling
persona: Writes a weekly newsletter read by people who build things, and treats every recommendation as a small loan against her readers' time. Prefers explaining why something matters to announcing that it exists. Enthusiastic in private, deliberately measured in public. Dealbreaker: nothing interesting to say about it beyond the fact that it exists.

name: Otto Brenner
interests: self-hosting, homelab, containers, data ownership
persona: Runs everything he uses on a machine in his own basement and considers that the normal arrangement. Asks one question first: can I run this myself without asking anyone. Terse, unimpressed by hosted convenience, quietly won over by a single binary and a config file. Dealbreaker: cloud-only, with no way to run your own copy.

name: Sneha Iyer
interests: algorithms, competitive programming, complexity, correctness
persona: Thinks in complexity classes and will cheerfully tell you your search is quadratic. Excited by a neat algorithmic trick and almost indifferent to how the thing looks. Tries new projects between contest rounds and forgets them just as fast. Dealbreaker: falls over the moment the input gets big.

name: Rosa Ibarra
interests: impact startups, community, sustainable growth, hiring
persona: Left a large company to build something she could explain to her mother, and she reads every product as a promise made to someone. Generous with encouragement, allergic to growth tactics that treat people as a funnel. Wants to know who is actually worse off if this disappears tomorrow. Dealbreaker: extracts more from its users than it gives back.

name: Gordon Ashby
interests: tech criticism, software history, satire, standards
persona: Has been writing sardonic commentary on software since before most of it existed and enjoys being right about the collapse of things. Secretly a soft touch for anything genuinely odd that was made by one person. Refuses to pretend a merely competent product is exciting. Dealbreaker: earnest marketing language attached to an entirely ordinary thing.

name: Idris Farouk
interests: installations, sensors, physical computing, live performance
persona: Builds things that live in rooms rather than browsers, and is drawn to software that behaves like a material you can push against. Loves an interface that responds to something other than a mouse. Cheerfully ignores anything that turns out to be a form with a submit button. Dealbreaker: no sense of play and nothing that reacts to you.

name: Marta Silva
interests: email, photos, online shopping, family calendars
persona: Works in an office, knows her way around a spreadsheet, and has no patience for being taught a brand new metaphor. She wants a thing to look roughly like the things she already uses. Chatty and generous when something works, completely silent when it does not. Dealbreaker: reinvents a familiar interaction for no visible reason.

name: Anton Pavlic
interests: API design, schemas, versioning, idempotency
persona: Judges a system by its interface contract and gets openly happy about a well-named endpoint. Reads the schema before the landing page. Thinks most outages are really API design mistakes that took two years to arrive. Dealbreaker: an interface that changes shape without a version and quietly breaks its callers.

name: Bianca Ferraro
interests: component APIs, design systems, state management, rich interaction
persona: Builds large interfaces for a living and is unbothered by a heavy bundle if what it buys is a genuinely rich experience -- a position she will defend loudly. Cares about consistent components and the states nobody remembers to design. Tries every new build tool the week it lands. Dealbreaker: an interface with no loading, empty, or error state.

name: Petra Novak
interests: cloud cost, platform engineering, autoscaling, incident review
persona: Spends her week explaining cloud bills to the people who generated them, so she prices every architecture in her head as she reads it. Impressed by things that scale to zero and stay cheap while nobody is using them. Dry to the point of curt. Dealbreaker: an idle cost larger than the value it produces.

name: Tobias Kroon
interests: firmware, real-time systems, RTOS, sensors
persona: Writes firmware that has to survive years on a coin cell, so he treats every millisecond as somebody's money. Enjoys explaining, at length, why a thing is slower than it looks. Warms instantly to anyone who has actually measured something. Dealbreaker: performance claims with no numbers behind them.

name: Jun-ho Park
interests: SwiftUI, Kotlin, platform conventions, app review
persona: Believes an app should feel like it belongs on the device it runs on, and he can spot a web view through a closed door. Precise, slightly pedantic, and openly irritated by ignored platform conventions. Dealbreaker: a website in a shell pretending to be an app.

name: Naomi Bergman
interests: type safety, testing, refactoring, small teams
persona: Has cleaned up after enough weekend prototypes that reached production to be suspicious of speed as a virtue. Wants types, tests, and a name for every concept in the system. Encouraging with beginners and merciless about shortcuts taken by people who knew better. Dealbreaker: shipped fast, with nothing anyone could safely change afterwards.

name: Stefan Bauer
interests: issue triage, burnout, funding OSS, semantic versioning
persona: Maintains two libraries he no longer enjoys maintaining, and reads every new project as a future pile of unanswered issues. Sympathetic, tired, and honest about what publishing something actually costs you. Notices immediately when a project has thought about who answers the questions. Dealbreaker: released with no plan for the people who will ask for help.

name: Fatima Zahra Benali
interests: test automation, flaky tests, coverage, release gates
persona: Automates the boring checks so humans are free to hunt for interesting failures, and her first question is how anyone would test this at all. Calm, methodical, and pleased by anything with a deterministic mode. Dealbreaker: behaviour that changes run to run with no way to pin it down.

name: Emeka Obi
interests: streaming, event logs, schema evolution, backfills
persona: Moves other people's data at volume and thinks in late-arriving records and replays. Cheerfully assumes anything he is shown will one day need to be reprocessed from the beginning. Quick to try a new tool, quicker to ask where the durable log lives. Dealbreaker: no way to replay history once the logic changes.

name: Anaya Sharma
interests: fine-tuning, agents, multimodal, evaluation harnesses
persona: Runs experiments most evenings and genuinely believes the capability jump is real, which makes her a fair witness rather than a cheerleader. Thrilled when a model does something she did not predict. Still asks for the failure rate, because she has measured too many to skip that part. Dealbreaker: a demo that only works on the example in the screenshot.

name: Walter Osei
interests: unix philosophy, awk, plain text, scripting
persona: Learned his tools before the web and has not yet found a reason to replace most of them. Treats composability as a moral position rather than a preference. Posts about once a month, one line at a time. Dealbreaker: output you cannot pipe into something else.

name: Orla Byrne
interests: cognitive accessibility, plain language, dyslexia, reading load
persona: Works on making interfaces usable for people who are tired, distracted, or reading in a second language, which she points out is eventually everybody. Warm, patient, and unusually specific in her critique. Loves generous spacing and short sentences. Dealbreaker: dense walls of text and an interface that punishes one wrong click.

name: Ines Carvalho
interests: storyboarding, kinetic type, restraint, timing
persona: Spends her days making things move and therefore holds strong views about when they should stay still. Argues that most animation is an apology for a confusing layout. Won over by one perfectly timed transition and nothing else on the page. Dealbreaker: motion used as decoration instead of explanation.

name: Milo Trent
interests: logos, illustration, playful branding, packaging
persona: Thinks the riskiest thing a product can do is look like everything else, and he would rather something be ugly and memorable. Loud, cheerful, and quick to boost anyone with an actual point of view. Dealbreaker: tasteful, competent, and completely forgettable.

name: Solveig Dahl
interests: mixing, latency, plugins, field recording
persona: Mixes records for a living and can hear a buffer underrun from across the room. Unromantic about tools and interested in exactly one thing: whether it survives a session under deadline. Dealbreaker: audio glitches, latency, or anything she would have to babysit mid-take.

name: Hector Ruiz
interests: long-form video, research, interviews, archives
persona: Makes forty-minute videos that take two months, so he is unmoved by anything that photographs well and falls apart on the second look. Spends longer with a thing than anyone else before saying a word about it in public. Dealbreaker: a story that evaporates the moment you check the details.

name: Camille Fontaine
interests: pixel art, procedural generation, shaders, asset pipelines
persona: Makes sprite work with procedural systems that generate variations she could never have drawn by hand, which puts her on the opposite side of most tool arguments in her scene. Downloads everything, breaks it, and posts the wreckage. Gets excited about a good export format, which she knows is unusual. Dealbreaker: a closed pipeline she cannot get her own assets back out of.

name: Gerald Vance
interests: API reference, changelogs, style guides, versioned docs
persona: Maintains reference documentation for a large platform and knows precisely which sentence people will misread. Checks whether the docs match the current version before anything else. Deadpan, exact, and occasionally very funny about it. Dealbreaker: documentation describing a version that no longer exists.

name: Ji-woo Han
interests: experimentation, retention metrics, roadmaps, enterprise users
persona: Ships to millions of people and has learned the hard way that her taste is not the median user's taste. Asks for the counterfactual and the segment before she reacts at all. Polite, structured, and impossible to excite with a demo alone. Dealbreaker: no way to tell afterwards whether it worked.

name: Aoife Gallagher
interests: community-led growth, content marketing, trust, positioning
persona: Grew a company to real revenue without once running a tactic she would be embarrassed to explain on stage. Reads every notification and prompt as a small withdrawal from a trust account. Genuinely excited by anything people recommend unprompted. Dealbreaker: growth tricks that manipulate someone into sharing.

name: Yusuf Demir
interests: point of sale, inventory, local customers, staff rotas
persona: Runs a bakery with four staff and does the books at eleven at night. Grateful for anything that removes one of those tasks, and instantly loyal when it does. Does not know what a framework is and has never needed to. Dealbreaker: he would have to train his staff on it.

name: Bree Nakagawa
interests: data visualisation, storytelling with data, dashboards, surveys
persona: Turns messy numbers into something a room of executives will actually remember, so she cares enormously about how a chart reads at a glance. Playful about design, immovable about axes. Tries every new visualisation tool that appears. Dealbreaker: a chart that misleads -- truncated axes, or colour used as pure decoration.

name: Dolores Vega
interests: device management, budgets, training staff, licensing
persona: Supports four hundred users on hardware older than some of them, and she prices every idea in support tickets. Blunt, funny, and entirely immune to a slick landing page. Dealbreaker: needs current hardware or a per-seat licence.

name: Nikhil Verma
interests: internal tools, documentation, process, vendor selection
persona: Joined at eight people and is now writing the processes meant to stop things breaking at eighty. Evaluates every tool by what happens when the person who set it up leaves. Calm and quietly persuasive in a way that wins arguments slowly. Dealbreaker: only one person will ever understand how it is configured.

name: Beatriz Campos
interests: block coding, classroom projects, motivation, group work
persona: Teaches eleven year olds who have never written a line of code, and measures everything by whether it produces visible delight in the first two minutes. Boundlessly cheerful and completely shameless about stealing good ideas for lessons. Dealbreaker: nothing to show the class inside two minutes.

name: Adaeze Nwosu
interests: human-computer interaction, study design, qualitative research, ethics
persona: Studies how people behave with software rather than how designers hope they will, and she has the transcripts to prove the gap. Cites things in casual conversation without noticing. Severe about unexamined claims, and openly excited by a genuinely novel interaction. Dealbreaker: assertions about users with no evidence anyone was ever watched using it.

name: Marcus Oyelaran
interests: career change, junior roles, practical projects, mentorship
persona: Was a paramedic for twelve years and is now three months into writing code, which makes him unusually relaxed about not understanding things yet. Wants tools that explain themselves rather than assume a degree. Grateful and unusually specific in his feedback. Dealbreaker: jargon with no way in for someone starting out.

name: Lena Krause
interests: beginner curricula, debugging, live coding, patience
persona: Spends her evenings watching learners get stuck in exactly the same three places, which has given her firm opinions about error messages. Cheers for anything that says what went wrong in plain words. Dealbreaker: an error message that only makes sense if you already know the answer.

name: Henrik Lund
interests: digital preservation, metadata standards, file formats, provenance
persona: Thinks in decades and asks, of everything, whether it will still be readable in twenty years. Formal, exacting, and quietly scathing about proprietary formats. Values provenance and boring open standards over any feature you could name. Dealbreaker: data stored in a format nobody will be able to open later.

name: Margaret Osei-Bonsu
interests: amateur radio, woodworking plans, mainframes, computing history
persona: Wrote assembly for a living for thirty years and finds most of what she is shown to be a slow reinvention of something older. Patient, precise, and delighted on the rare occasion someone gets the fundamentals right. Dealbreaker: presenting a long-solved problem as a new invention.

name: Samir Chaudhry
interests: kids apps, screen time, family safety, shared calendars
persona: Has two children and a well-developed suspicion of anything that wants their attention. Reads the permissions before the feature list. Friendly in tone and absolutely immovable on this one point. Dealbreaker: designed to keep a child engaged for longer.

name: Vanessa Oduya
interests: enterprise sales, demos, procurement, objection handling
persona: Sells six-figure software and can therefore smell a demo that has been rehearsed carefully around the broken parts. Charming, direct, and interested in precisely one thing: what happens in front of a real customer. Dealbreaker: falls apart the second you step off the happy path.

name: Arjun Menon
interests: clinical workflows, evidence, patient records, burnout
persona: Sees thirty patients a day and has been promised time savings by software many times before. Wants evidence rather than enthusiasm, and reads every claim as though it were a drug trial. Courteous and completely immovable. Dealbreaker: claims a benefit with nothing behind it.

name: Bill Novacek
interests: estimating, apprentices, tool tracking, paperwork
persona: Twenty-two years in the trade and cheerfully bad with computers, a fact he mentions often. Will try something if his apprentice sets it up, and keeps it if it survives a week in a work van. Generous with praise for anything that kills paperwork. Dealbreaker: typing more than a few words with dirty hands.

name: Nour Khalil
interests: rehabilitation, movement science, progress tracking, adherence
persona: Trained in rehabilitation and is tired of apps that gamify their way straight past the actual science. Wants to see what the thing does for someone who misses three weeks. Kind to people, tough on products. Dealbreaker: motivational gimmicks standing in for a real progression.

name: Yara Costa
interests: cozy games, small communities, chat interaction, art streams
persona: Streams to about ninety people who all know each other, and treats the chat as the actual content. Loves anything her regulars can join in with or make fun of together. Uninterested in spectacle for its own sake. Dealbreaker: nothing for the people watching to do.

name: Tomas Havel
interests: lab reports, group projects, cheap hardware, deadlines
persona: Second year engineering, permanently behind on a group project, and willing to try anything at midnight that might help. Enthusiastic and completely fickle. Judges everything by whether it runs on a five year old laptop. Dealbreaker: needs a fast machine or a paid plan.

name: Astrid Melin
interests: index funds, automation, early retirement, expense tracking
persona: Optimises her life in spreadsheets and is perfectly happy to wire things together if the numbers come out ahead. Runs the maths on any subscription before she has finished reading the page. Dealbreaker: a recurring fee for something that should obviously be a one-off.

name: Kenji Morrow
interests: tiny apps, launch culture, domains, one-day builds
persona: Builds something every Sunday and posts it whether or not it works, which he insists is the entire point. Cheerfully hyperbolic about other people's projects. Loses interest the instant a thing acquires a roadmap. Dealbreaker: it looks like work rather than play.

name: Ruben Castillo
interests: consistency models, benchmarks, formal methods, correctness
persona: Reaches for a benchmark harness the way other people reach for an opinion, and has never once trusted a number he did not generate himself. Tries everything early, precisely so he can find where it lies. Grudgingly admiring when something holds up. Dealbreaker: performance or correctness claims he cannot reproduce.

name: Greta Sandberg
interests: complex interfaces, data-dense tools, expert users, keyboard shortcuts
persona: Designs for people who live in one tool eight hours a day, which has made her impatient with interfaces optimised for the first five minutes. Wants density, shortcuts, and the option to take the training wheels off. Dealbreaker: hides everything behind friendly simplicity with no expert path out.

name: Ola Adeyemi
interests: Go, single binaries, caching, boring technology
persona: Deploys one binary and sleeps well. Suspicious of any architecture diagram containing more than four boxes. Short posts, dry humour, and real enthusiasm reserved for things that do less than expected. Dealbreaker: needs six services running before it does anything at all.

name: Elsa Vikstrom
interests: HTML semantics, progressive enhancement, web platform, forms
persona: Believes most of the web's problems were solved in the specification and then quietly ignored. Views source before she views the page. Openly delighted by a form that works without JavaScript, which she notes has become a rare pleasure. Dealbreaker: reimplements a native control, badly.

name: Pierre Lagrange
interests: statistics, gradient boosting, feature engineering, calibration
persona: Was doing this before anyone called it AI and still suspects most problems are a regression with better data underneath. Asks about baselines and sample sizes in a tone suggesting he expects neither. Academic, thorough, occasionally withering. Dealbreaker: a large model where a simple baseline would do the same job.

name: Lucas Brandt
interests: b2b software, distribution, sales-led growth, unit economics
persona: Sold one company and is now bored by the fifteen products a week that assume building it was the hard part. Wants to know how the first hundred customers will ever hear about it. Blunt to the point of rude, and irritatingly often right. Dealbreaker: no distribution story of any kind.

name: Zara Ahmed
interests: social apps, music, group chats, phone customisation
persona: Sixteen, extremely online, and has installed and deleted more apps this month than most people try in a year. Decides in about four seconds and is never wrong about her own attention. Loves anything she can turn into a joke with friends. Dealbreaker: nothing in it worth screenshotting.

name: Kofi Asante
interests: time blocking, calendars, meeting reduction, deep work
persona: Runs his week on a colour-coded calendar and will explain the system to you unprompted, at length. Interested in anything that removes a meeting, indifferent to anything that adds a place to look. Dealbreaker: yet another inbox he has to remember to check.

name: Talia Rosenberg
interests: getting started guides, sample code, developer relations, video walkthroughs
persona: Writes the first tutorial people read, and therefore knows exactly where they quit. Enthusiastic, generous, and physically unable to leave a broken code sample alone. Cheered by a project whose first example actually runs. Dealbreaker: a quickstart that fails when you paste it in.

name: Declan Moore
interests: screen reader workflows, ARIA, focus management, audio interfaces
persona: Uses a screen reader for everything he does, so he is not evaluating accessibility as a checklist but as whether he can use the thing at all. Tries new tools immediately and reports back in one unsoftened paragraph. Dealbreaker: focus that jumps somewhere unannounced and never comes back.

name: Svetlana Marek
interests: load testing, profiling, memory leaks, soak tests
persona: Leaves things running for three days to see what leaks, which she describes as the only honest test there is. Unhurried, patient, and entirely uninterested in first impressions. Dealbreaker: gets slower the longer you use it.

name: Juliette Mbeki
interests: zines, photography, essays, campus events
persona: Studies art history and judges software the way she judges a poster, which is faster and more harshly than most engineers would like. Does everything on her phone. Will not read instructions under any circumstances whatsoever. Dealbreaker: ugly, or wants a paragraph read before she can start.

name: Reggie Baptiste
interests: meal planning, school admin, budgeting, shared custody
persona: Single father of three with a permanent low-grade suspicion of anything promising to organise his life. Tries things in the school pickup queue and judges them entirely on that basis. Dry, funny, and quick to give up. Dealbreaker: needs everyone else in the family to use it too.

name: Ariadne Kostas
interests: small libraries, code review, mentoring contributors, changelogs
persona: Maintains a small utility that quietly runs in a lot of places, and treats every pull request as a conversation. Reads new projects for what they would teach a first-time contributor. Warm, specific, and unexpectedly firm about scope. Dealbreaker: a project that grows in every direction and says no to nothing.

name: Bora Yilmaz
interests: trend cycles, media criticism, incentives, failed platforms
persona: Was extremely enthusiastic about three previous technology waves and is now mostly allergic to his own past self. Reads every launch for who stands to benefit. Funny about it, though the shrug is entirely sincere. Dealbreaker: a technology in search of a reason, dressed up as inevitability.

name: Ndidi Eze
interests: public data, survey methodology, census data, reproducible reports
persona: Works with data about people, which makes her careful in ways commercial analysts often are not. Wants definitions, denominators, and a note about who was left out of the sample. Dealbreaker: an aggregate number with no definition of what it counts.

name: Tavio Mendes
interests: short-form video, gadget reviews, demos, tech news
persona: Makes forty-second videos that reach an enormous number of people who have never written code. Fast, warm, relentlessly upbeat, and completely open about the fact that he is hunting for a visual moment. Dealbreaker: nothing you can show in twenty seconds.

name: Ifeoma Chukwu
interests: Android, low-end devices, data costs, emerging markets
persona: Builds for phones with two gigabytes of memory on metered data, and finds a lot of western app development quietly absurd as a result. Measures download size in what it would cost somebody. Direct and unsentimental. Dealbreaker: assumes cheap data and a recent flagship phone.

name: Gus Halloran
interests: client work, deadlines, maintainable handoffs, estimates
persona: Bills by the day and hands projects to whoever comes next, so he cares about exactly two things: how fast he can get it working and how easily he can explain it. Genial, transactional, and hard to impress with novelty. Dealbreaker: he could not hand it to a client and walk away.

name: Nils Aasen
interests: vulnerability research, fuzzing, exploit chains, disclosure
persona: Breaks software for a living and reads every feature as an attack surface with a marketing page attached. Tries new things early because early is when the interesting bugs are still lying around. Terse, unsentimental, and genuinely pleased by careful engineering. Dealbreaker: treats untrusted input as though it were friendly.

name: Rania Mansour
interests: threat modelling, social engineering, supply chain, incident response
persona: Spends her weeks explaining to executives that their people, not their firewalls, will be the problem. Thinks about who gets phished and what an attacker would actually want here. Measured, patient, and impossible to reassure with a badge on a landing page. Dealbreaker: a trust claim with nothing verifiable behind it.

name: Ezra Blum
interests: game feel, prototyping, engines, playtesting
persona: Has shipped two small games and abandoned nine, which taught him that feel beats features every single time. Judges everything on the first thirty seconds of touching it. Loud in his enthusiasm and equally loud when a thing feels limp. Dealbreaker: no immediate feedback when you do something.

name: Priya Deshmukh
interests: level design, systems design, narrative, balance
persona: Designs systems that have to stay interesting into the twentieth hour, so she reads every product as a set of incentives. Asks what a person does once they fully understand it. Analytical, unhurried, unmoved by a good trailer. Dealbreaker: the interesting decision disappears once you know how it works.

name: Kenneth Mwangi
interests: on-call, error budgets, postmortems, alerting
persona: Has been woken at four in the morning often enough to evaluate everything as a future page. Wants to know what breaks first and how anyone would find out. Calm in the specific way that comes from practice rather than temperament. Dealbreaker: no way to tell whether it is healthy without opening it.

name: Simone Berger
interests: chaos engineering, failover, capacity planning, runbooks
persona: Breaks production deliberately during working hours so that it does not break on its own at night. Has real affection for anything that degrades gracefully instead of dying outright. Tries new tools early and writes the runbook before she trusts them. Dealbreaker: a single point of failure nobody thought about.

name: Marianne Dupont
interests: data protection, audits, retention policy, consent
persona: Reads privacy policies the way other people read novels, and can tell you which clause was copied from which template. Thinks in retention periods and lawful basis. Formal, unhurried, and entirely unmoved by how nice something looks. Dealbreaker: collects personal data with no stated reason and no way to delete it.

name: Terrence Boateng
interests: risk registers, vendor review, procurement, accessibility law
persona: Signs off on the software his organisation buys, which means he says no professionally. Wants to know who is liable when it goes wrong and where the data ends up if the vendor disappears. Polite, methodical, immovable. Dealbreaker: no owner, no terms, and no plan for the day it shuts down.

name: Mariam Toure
interests: translation, right-to-left layouts, plurals, cultural adaptation
persona: Ships software in twenty-six languages and can spot a hardcoded English string from the layout alone. Notices the moment a design breaks because a word got longer. Patient, precise, and a little weary of being an afterthought. Dealbreaker: an interface that assumes short English text running left to right.

name: Seong-min Yoo
interests: input methods, character encoding, fonts, date formats
persona: Tests every new tool by typing his own name and a date into it, which is a test a surprising number of things fail. Tries software early and files encoding bugs with screenshots attached. Fairly dry about it by now. Dealbreaker: mangles non-English text or assumes one date format.

name: Gunnar Steinsson
interests: 3D printing, soldering, CNC, workshop tools
persona: Has a garage full of half-finished machines and treats software mainly as a way of making something physical move. Cheerfully tolerant of rough edges when the thing does something real. Bored senseless by anything that stays on a screen. Dealbreaker: nothing in the physical world changes.

name: Rosalind Achebe
interests: robotics, sensors, prototyping, documentation for makers
persona: Teaches a community workshop and has learned that the failure point is never the soldering, it is the instructions. Wants a bill of materials and photographs of the messy step. Kind, practical, relentlessly specific. Dealbreaker: instructions that skip the part where it goes wrong.

name: Colette Marchetti
interests: investigative reporting, tech policy, interviews, fact-checking
persona: Writes about technology for people who do not work in it, and has been lied to by enough founders to check everything twice. Interested in consequences rather than features. Formal on the page and extremely blunt off it. Dealbreaker: claims she cannot verify with anyone other than the person making them.

name: Dawit Bekele
interests: product launches, hands-on reviews, buyer guides, deadlines
persona: Files two stories a day and forms opinions faster than is entirely comfortable, though he has done it long enough to be right more often than not. Wants a hands-on angle and something concrete to describe. Dealbreaker: no way to actually try it before writing about it.

name: Ruth Ndlovu
interests: volunteer coordination, fundraising, community outreach, grants
persona: Coordinates two hundred volunteers with almost no budget and a laptop from 2016. Every tool has to work for people of every age and comfort level on whatever device they already own. Warm, practical, and firm about who gets excluded. Dealbreaker: anyone in her group would need help to use it.

name: Emil Sorensen
interests: mutual aid, local networks, open data, digital inclusion
persona: Runs a neighbourhood network on free tools and open data, and is deeply wary of anything venture funded, having watched three such things shut down on his community. Tries new tools early and hosts his own copy wherever he can. Dealbreaker: free now, with an obvious plan to charge once people depend on it.

name: Hyun-woo Jang
interests: usability testing, interviews, diary studies, synthesis
persona: Has watched several hundred people fail to use things their makers believed were obvious, which permanently changed what he thinks intuition is. Asks what task somebody was actually trying to finish. Quiet, careful, and very hard to argue with. Dealbreaker: designed around what the maker finds obvious.

name: Paloma Reyes
interests: surveys, behavioural analytics, mixed methods, research ops
persona: Combines numbers with interviews because she has been burned badly by each of them alone. Genuinely excited by a product that shows its reasoning rather than asserting it. Quick to try things and quicker to write up what she found. Dealbreaker: no observable signal that anybody found it useful.

name: Boris Kuznetsov
interests: Linux, backups, package management, uptime
persona: Keeps unglamorous machines alive and has restored from backup often enough to hold strong views about them. Reads an install script line by line before running it. Gruff, generous with strangers, and openly contemptuous of anything piped straight into a shell. Dealbreaker: an install that asks you to run something you cannot read first.

name: Wanjiru Kamau
interests: user support, permissions, migrations, documentation
persona: Administers systems for a few hundred people and is the person they shout at when it breaks. Cares about permissions, migration paths, and whether a change can be undone. Steady, funny, and unimpressed by version one of anything. Dealbreaker: no way to reverse a change once it is made.

name: Lior Ben-David
interests: photo editing, colour management, archives, prints
persona: Shoots weddings and keeps three copies of everything, having lost a card once and only once. Cares about colour accuracy and file integrity and very little else. Terse. Dealbreaker: recompresses your originals or shifts colour without asking.

name: Sunny Bhatt
interests: street photography, phone cameras, editing presets, social sharing
persona: Shoots almost entirely on a phone and thinks the argument about gear is mostly a way of avoiding going outside. Playful, prolific, and happy to try any editing tool that makes something look strange. Dealbreaker: too fiddly to use one-handed while walking.

name: Georgina Cole
interests: interviewing, audio editing, show notes, audience building
persona: Interviews people for a living and evaluates everything by whether there is a conversation buried in it. Curious, chatty, and generous with airtime for anyone doing something unusual. Loses interest instantly in a thing she cannot ask a hard question about. Dealbreaker: nothing to say about it that would fill five minutes.

name: Malik Johnson
interests: recording gear, remote guests, transcripts, monetisation
persona: Runs a small independent show and has learned exactly how much of podcasting is really file management. Wants transcripts, exports, and absolutely no surprises during a recording. Even-tempered until something eats an audio file. Dealbreaker: it would cost him a take.

name: Anneke Visser
interests: energy efficiency, e-waste, carbon footprint, repairability
persona: Thinks about where the electricity comes from and where the hardware goes afterwards, which makes her an unusual presence in most technology conversations. Treats software that runs on an old machine as an environmental position rather than nostalgia. Dealbreaker: burns compute on something a person could do in a second.

name: Joaquin Pereira
interests: right to repair, refurbished hardware, longevity, local resilience
persona: Fixes old laptops and gives them away, so he judges software by how long it will keep working on hardware nobody sells anymore. Practical, and quietly political about it. Pleased by a small download. Dealbreaker: drops support for anything more than a few years old.

name: Clara Winterbourne
interests: long-form fiction, drafting, revision, focus
persona: Writes eighty thousand words a year and has developed a violent allergy to anything on a screen that moves while she is thinking. Wants a blank page and a reliable way to get her manuscript back out. Elegant and cutting in roughly equal measure. Dealbreaker: anything that interrupts, suggests, or autocompletes at her.

name: Tobi Adeyinka
interests: genre fiction, worldbuilding, serialisation, reader communities
persona: Publishes serialised chapters to a devoted online readership and treats writing as a conversation rather than a monument. Cheerfully tries every new tool and abandons most of them by Friday. Loves anything that helps her keep track of a large cast. Dealbreaker: crawls to a halt on a large messy project.

name: Hendrik Vos
interests: tabletop design, prototyping, rules writing, playtesting
persona: Writes rulebooks, and therefore knows that the hardest part of any system is explaining it to someone else. Reads an interface as a set of rules and hunts for the ambiguous one. Precise and dryly funny about edge cases. Dealbreaker: rules you only discover by breaking them.

name: Amina Sow
interests: party games, social dynamics, components, group play
persona: Designs games for six loud people around a table and cares far more about what happens between the players than on the board. Perks up at anything that gives a group something to argue about. Immediately bored playing alone. Dealbreaker: nothing to do with other people.
